canonical_sources.title: Basic Facts & Figures, Numbers of Dead and Injured, Bhopal Disaster (consulted 2026-11-02)
After 40 years, hazardous waste from Union Carbide plant shifted out of Bhopal (consulted 2026-11-02)

pedagogy.problem_statement: A pesticide plant beside a city of nearly 900,000 people, and a night when its safeguards did not work.
pedagogy.core_thesis: On the night of 2-3 December 1984 about 30 tonnes of methyl isocyanate escaped from the Union Carbide India plant in Bhopal; the safety systems were failing, the death toll is still disputed, and justice was partial.
pedagogy.mental_model: One sheet of paper: a plant drawn as a schematic, an ink stain that leaks out of it and never dries, and ledger entries written onto the stain.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: Bhopal is not finished: nobody agrees how many died, the legal outcomes were limited, and over 100,000 survivors still live with chronic illness.
verified_claims: The leak occurred on the night of 2-3 December 1984; pressure rose from about 10:30 p.m., the reaction became critical around 12:40 a.m., and the leak stopped at about 2 a.m. [Wikipedia, Bhopal disaster].
The gas was methyl isocyanate (MIC), held in underground tank E610, which contained 42 tons of liquid MIC when the reaction began [Wikipedia].
About 30 tonnes escaped in 45-60 minutes; sources vary and some put the total near 40 tonnes within two hours [Wikipedia].
MIC was an intermediate in the manufacture of Sevin (carbaryl), a pesticide [Wikipedia].

The plant belonged to Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL); Union Carbide Corporation held a majority stake and the rest (49.1%) was held by the Indian public and government-controlled banks [Wikipedia].
Bhopal's population at the time was 894,539 [bhopal.org, citing MP BGRR].

Refrigeration of the MIC tank was shut down in January 1982; the vent gas scrubber was on standby with insufficient caustic soda and power; the flare tower had a pipe removed and was improperly sized for the leak [Wikipedia, citing UCC's own report and investigations].
The public siren sounded briefly at about 12:50 a.m. and was turned off per company procedure [Wikipedia].

How water entered the tank is disputed: critics point to a side pipe during cleaning and poor maintenance; Union Carbide says a disgruntled employee connected a hose. Investigators could not reproduce the pipe route in tests [Wikipedia].
More than 500,000 people were exposed [Wikipedia infobox].

Government-confirmed deaths: 3,787 (Madhya Pradesh government). Immediate official count: 2,259. Survivor-group estimate: 22,917 to about 23,000 (BGIA / ICMR-derived). Other estimates range from 8,000 in the first weeks to over 25,000 in total [Wikipedia, bhopal.org]. No single figure is established.
In 1989 Union Carbide paid US$470 million in an out-of-court settlement, upheld by the Indian Supreme Court in 1991 [Wikipedia].
In June 2010 seven former UCIL employees were convicted of causing death by negligence and sentenced to two years; an eighth died before sentencing [Wikipedia].
Warren Anderson, UCC chief executive at the time, was declared a fugitive by an Indian court in 1992; the US declined extradition; he died on 29 September 2014 aged 92 [Wikipedia].
On 14 March 2023 the Indian Supreme Court dismissed a curative petition seeking enhanced compensation [Wikipedia].

In January 2025, about 337 tonnes of hazardous waste (other reports say 307-377 tonnes) was moved from the Bhopal plant site to a disposal facility at Pithampur, roughly 250 km away [Scroll.in and other 2025 reports; quantities vary by outlet].

A 2023 report put the number still suffering chronic illness at more than 120,000, per the state relief department [Free Press Journal, 2023, via search summary]; the film says 'more than a hundred thousand'.
anti_patterns: Do not state any single death toll as the truth; always attribute (government vs survivor groups).
Do not say water entry was an accident or sabotage; say it is disputed.
Do not state 'soil and groundwater are still contaminated' as a 2026 fact without a current source; the 2025 waste removal is the verified present-day anchor.
Do not name or depict real victims or show bodies.
Do not claim a specific death count for 'the first night'; use 'within days, thousands'.
Details of the railway station staff's actions are inconsistent across sources; they are left out.

scene_blueprint.title: A city falling asleep
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Date, place, scale of the city, the plant at its edge
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Schematic of the plant draws on; a cloud-shaped ink stain begins at the vent and the camera drops onto a skyline of lit windows

scene_blueprint.title: The tank and the failing safeguards
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: What was in the tank and that pressure began to rise; Water ingress is disputed; safeguards were not working
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Cutaway of tank E610 in line art; a pressure needle creeps up; 42 tons label Then: Three safeguard icons are each crossed through with a pen stroke; a question mark hangs over the water pipe

scene_blueprint.title: The cloud and the waking
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: 30 tonnes escape over the sleeping streets; the siren is switched off; People wake and flee; thousands dead within days
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Ochre ink blooms from the vent and soaks the skyline; windows go out one by one; a single siren tone cuts Then: Small ink figures run through the stained streets; 'thousands' lands as a ledger line

scene_blueprint.title: Nobody agrees
scene_blueprint.visual_action: A ledger writes 3,787 and a dot field fills the page well beyond it toward about 23,000

scene_blueprint.title: Partial justice
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: 1989 settlement, 2010 convictions, Anderson never faced an Indian court
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Ledger stamps: US$470 million, seven figures with 2 years, an empty chair outline

scene_blueprint.title: Still here
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Waste removed January 2025; over 100,000 still ill; the night has not ended
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Trucks leave the plant outline; dawn skyline with a few windows lit; the stain remains; hold
